newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET-YOUNG SCORES 73 BUT MATCH ENDS IN DRAW.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-YOUNG SCORES 73 BUT MATCH ENDS IN DRAW.

text.p: Bryan Young made a
solid 73 as New Zealand's cricketers drew their tour-opening
three-day match against a Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) XI on
Tuesday.
The Northern Districts right-hander batted with
determination to emerge the top scorer again after his first
innings knock of 47.
He figured in two useful partnerships, putting on 76 for the
second wicket with Justin Vaughan and 61 with Stephen Fleming
for the fourth wicket after the tourists resumed their second
innings at 34 for one.
New Zealand, 171 in the first innings, conceded a nominal 22
runs' lead as the PCB XI responded with 193 for seven declared.
Young batted for 258 minutes and hit nine fours from 163
balls while Vaughan took his score from 21 to 48, which included
five fours from 113 balls.
Fleming contributed 27 before falling lbw to paceman
Mohammad Zahid, New Zealand's first innings tormentor.
His wicket was among the four that fell cheaply in a space
of 24 runs as the middle order collapsed once again with Adam
Parore (four), Mark Greatbatch (two) and Gavin Larsen (one)
getting out easily.
Nathan Astle was on 30 and Matthew Hart nine when Greatbatch
declared the second innings closed at 211 for seven half an hour
after tea, leaving the PCB XI 190 to win in an hour.
PCB XI captain and test bowler Aaqib Javed was the most
successful bowler with three for 38 from 17 overs while Zahid
captured two for 40 for a match figures of eight for 94.
When the match ended, the local side had reached 41 without
loss in 15 overs with Zahoor Elahi on 23 and Mohammad Wasim 14.
New Zealand now face Pakistan in the first test starting at
Lahore on Thursday.
